key_insight: The paper shows how to estimate the exact posterior score for linear inverse problems, instead of relying on approximate guidance from an unconditional diffusion prior. This makes posterior sampling more faithful to the measurement data while preserving the benefits of pretrained generative priors.
problem_solved: How to use diffusion or flow-based models to solve linear inverse problems by sampling from the true posterior, rather than only using the unconditional data prior or approximate measurement corrections.
method: Derives a way to obtain the posterior score needed for inverse problem sampling.
Bridges pretrained denoising priors with measurement consistency, avoiding the need to retrain a fully conditional restoration model.
Maintains the denoising structure of diffusion/flow models while targeting exact posterior inference.
impact: For practitioners, this can improve reconstruction quality in tasks like imaging, deblurring, denoising, and compressed sensing by making generative priors more accurate and measurement-aware. It also reduces the gap between powerful pretrained generative models and reliable inverse-problem solvers.
